purpose: Teach: 断固/刻ま/在学/将校/忠誠/一変/苦難/体格

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、論文、戦時の政府、断固たる姿勢、丁寧に、論じていますね、本当に、印象的でした、本気で。
lines.en: Ren — your paper on wartime government policy was impressively thorough. The way you handled such a difficult subject with such care really struck me.
lines.style: Warm, steady approval. Deliberate pace. She's choosing her words carefully because she means them. Slight lean forward—this is genuine recognition, not performative praise.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。慰霊碑に刻まれた名前、本当に、現代に、語りかけるような、力、感じました、本気で、感動的でした。
lines.en: Thank you. When I saw those names carved into the memorial, it felt like they were speaking directly to the present. That sense of connection really moved me—it made the research matter.
lines.style: Quiet intensity. He's not trying to perform earnestness; it rises naturally from him. Slight catch in his voice on 'speaking to the present.' Measured, like he's still working through what he felt.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 当時、大学に在学中の若者、本当に、戦地に、送られた歴史、論文で、扱っていますね、辛い、内容でしたよね。
lines.en: It must have been difficult to write about young people your own age being sent to war. You handled that weight carefully.
lines.style: Reflective, slightly softer. Not pitying—observant. She's acknowledging the emotional labour without making him uncomfortable. Pace slows slightly, giving space to the weight of the subject.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。将校たちの記録、論文の重要な、史料、本気で、貴重な、研究、できました、本当に、深い、研究でした、絶対。
lines.en: Yes. The officers' records I found were invaluable—they really became the backbone of my argument. I was able to do something genuinely substantive with them.
lines.style: More confidence here. He's talking about the work itself now, not the feeling. Slight lift on 'invaluable' and 'backbone'—pride in the research, not arrogance. Still measured but assured.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 忠誠心という、概念、戦中、本当に、強かったんですよね、論文の中で、丁寧に、扱われていました、本気で、印象的。
lines.en: The concept of loyalty during wartime—you unpacked that so carefully. How it shaped everything about that period. That was really striking work.
lines.style: Engaged, conversational but precise. She's leaning in slightly on 'unpacked'—respecting the intellectual weight. Warm but not effusive. Each phrase lands with intention.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。戦中、戦後で、社会が、一変、しましたね、論文の核心、テーマでした、本気で、深い、研究、できました、絶対。
lines.en: Yes, exactly. The transformation from wartime to post-war society—that rupture was really the heart of what I was trying to understand. It changed everything about how people thought, how they survived.
lines.style: Building energy—this is where his real investment shows. Not rushed, but more alive. He's seeing the argument clearly now as he speaks it. Words come a little faster because he's remembering why it mattered.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 戦後の苦難、人々が、どう乗り越えたか、論文で、本当に、丁寧に、扱っていましたね、桜さん、本気で、立派。
lines.en: And the way you wrote about how people endured the hardship after the war—there was real dignity in that section. It wasn't just analysis. You honoured their struggle.
lines.style: Warmth deepens. Slower pace here. She's seen something in his work that goes beyond academic skill. Slight drop in volume on 'honoured'—that's the real compliment, and she knows it. Sincere without being sentimental.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。戦中、人々の体格、栄養不足で、変化したという、史料、論文に、引用しました、本気で、貴重な、視点でした、絶対。
lines.en: Thank you. I found records showing how physical conditions changed—malnutrition left visible marks across the population. Using that data felt important because it made the human cost concrete, not abstract.
lines.style: Quiet authority. He's moved past nervousness now. Speaking as someone who has genuinely understood his subject. No filler, no hedging. Slight emphasis on 'concrete'—that was the turning point for him. Grounded and clear.
